question_bank.stem: A team is building an audio-monitoring product, but repeated prompt changes on a text-first setup have stalled. Based on the lecture, what is the better next move?

options.text: Keep refining prompts, because text-centric prompting usually transfers cleanly to raw audio tasks.
Move toward direct deep-learning methods for the audio signal, because that modality often needs more than prompting.
Switch to decision trees, because audio tasks benefit most from smaller non-neural models as data grows.
Pause modeling and reorganize the database, because modality choice matters less than system design.

question_bank.rationale: Ng says prompting is strongest for text, while audio and similar modalities often still call for direct deep-learning methods.

source_ref.evidence_span: algorithms directly when I'm working with audio data, image

frame_evidence.visual_description: Handwritten side list of modalities on the board near the CS/ML/DL stack, matching the contrast between text prompting and non-text data.

question_bank.stem: A student wants the Stanford AI class most centered on building deep-learning systems rather than a broad, math-heavy ML survey. Which course best matches that goal?

options.text: CS129, because it is the broadest survey and the most theory intensive.
CS229, because it focuses just on deep learning and minimizes mathematical analysis.
Either CS129 or CS229, because the lecture treated them as overlapping practical deep-learning tracks.
CS230, because the lecture framed it as the applied course focused on deep learning.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture positions CS230 as the more applied deep-learning course, while CS229 is broader and more mathematical.

source_ref.evidence_span: and it focuses just on deep learning.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Instructor points to handwritten course labels on the board while comparing CS129, CS229, and CS230.

question_bank.stem: For a mostly text-based product, which starting strategy did Ng describe as usually effective before going deeper?

options.text: Begin with prompting, because text-based applications often go quite far with that approach.
Begin with direct vision-style architectures, because text is the least natural fit for transformer prompting.
Begin by collecting multimodal audio-video corpora, because text systems usually need extra modalities to work.
Begin by avoiding GenAI altogether, because prompt-based systems rarely help on language tasks.

question_bank.rationale: He says transformer-based GenAI is really fantastic for text-based applications, so prompting is often the right first move there.

source_ref.evidence_span: and so on, really fantastic for text-based applications.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Board still shows the nearby modality comparison used during the discussion of where prompting works best.
